🔻 Iran’s Kanoon urges UNICEF to pursue justice for war-hit children

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran’s Institute for the Intellectual Development of Children and Young Adults (IIDCYA), better known as Kanoon, has called on the United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund (UNICEF) to publicly condemn attacks that killed or injured Iranian children and pursue accountability for violations of their rights.

In a letter marking World Children’s Day on Friday, Kanoon’s director, Hamed Alamati, addressed UNICEF Executive Director Catherine Russell, seeking investigations into the attacks and a comprehensive plan to provide psychological and social support for affected children.
​
Alamati recalled the US-Israeli acts of aggression against Iran, which began on February 28, 2026, and described the strike on a school in Minab as a grave violation of international humanitarian law. He said children had been deprived of their right to life and education.
​
The letter also referred to the killing of 14-month-old Zahra Mohammadi Golpayegani, who died alongside her grandfather, martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei.
​
Citing a July 31 statement by UNICEF’s regional office, Alamati said 386 children had been reported killed and 2,117 injured in Iran over five months. He stressed that surviving children needed opportunities to grieve, receive support and return to safe classrooms.
​
He urged UNICEF to cooperate with relevant UN bodies in documenting violations, verifying evidence and informing families of the findings.
​
The institute also offered its libraries, educators and artistic programs to help affected children resume educational and cultural activities, requesting a written response outlining planned measures and the official responsible for following up.
